definition: A muscle action potential is the electrical response recorded from a muscle when its nerve is stimulated. In this context, it is measured as a compound muscle action potential, which reflects the combined activity of the muscle’s functioning motor units and is used in estimating motor unit number.

reasons: The packet supports compound muscle action potential (CMAP), not the broader term “muscle action potential,” so the entry appears to use the wrong sense/term.

The claim that this is “the electrical response recorded from a muscle when its nerve is stimulated” is not stated in the packet as a definition; the packet only says CMAPs were recorded after peroneal nerve stimulation and used in MUNE.

“Reflects the combined activity of the muscle’s functioning motor units” is an unsupported paraphrase; the packet says MUNE estimates motor units by dividing maximal CMAP size by mean surface-recorded motor unit potential size, but does not define CMAP this way.

The definition centers on the term “muscle action potential,” but the packet discusses “compound muscle action potential (CMAP)” and “surface-recorded motor unit potential (SMUP)” in the context of motor unit number estimation; it does not define “muscle action potential” as such or equate the two terms.

The packet does not explicitly state that the CMAP “reflects the combined activity of the muscle’s functioning motor units” in those exact terms (it describes using maximal CMAP size within a premise/ratio for MUNE, but not that specific phrasing of combined motor-unit activity).

While the packet supports that CMAP size is used in motor unit number estimation (MUNE) by relating maximal CMAP size to mean SMUP size, the definition’s overall “muscle action potential → CMAP” framing is not directly supported.
